contract_answer.question: Does the registered degradation-law loss at rho 0.5 reduce held-out law-fit excess over the true-EOL floor by at least 30% without split-2021 MAPE above 0.1049 or BALANCE_FAIL?
contract_answer.conclusion: Reviewer recomputation from all 600 selected-checkpoint predictions matches the lead: best epoch 5 of 13, MAPE 0.101724, Acc@15 0.791667, RMSE 22.1053 cycles, bias -13.1014 cycles, and prediction/target spread 0.72046. The parent NA-E009 values are 0.099874, 0.743333, 22.5282, -15.9075, and 0.74972. Prefix-band MAPE is 0.1451/0.0941/0.0986/0.0932/0.1007 versus 0.1221/0.0936/0.0928/0.0932/0.1085. Balance passes at calibrated lambda 0.089016 (median R 0.594; cosine +0.577 then +0.983; active fraction 0.953 then 0.688), and MAPE passes the 0.1049 ceiling. However, held-out law-fit error is 0.0444 versus parent 0.0463 and floor 0.0161: excess falls only about 6%, not the required 30% (error <= 0.0372). The pre-registered rule therefore requires DISCARD.

main_symptom: The degradation-law objective materially improves Acc@15 and slightly improves RMSE and bias, but scarcely changes its defining held-out physics metric: law-fit excess falls only about 6% versus the required 30%, while overall MAPE rises by 0.00185 and 1-10 MAPE rises by 0.0230.

next_action.summary: DISCARD this rho 0.5 configuration under its pre-registered physics rule, but classify degradation-law loss as promising under A2 because Acc@15 improves by 0.0483 with only +0.00185 MAPE and -0.42-cycle RMSE change, satisfying path C. Use the single loss.md 5.3 repair on rho only: test rho 1.0. Median R 0.59 leaves room (nominally about 1.19), both measured cosines are positive, and active fraction is still 0.69 at step 61, so stronger law pressure is evidence-led; the early selected epoch 5 makes further strengthening beyond this one capped test unwarranted.
